run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log severity and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested `terms: {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]}` query against index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned 0 hits, both in the default 1h range and over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T06:48:03Z–2026-11-21T06:48:03Z. The index mapping contains no `level` field at all: its only fields are `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer) and `svc` (keyword). Re-running the query on the actual severity field, `severity_num`, with the numeric codes that correspond to ERROR (5) and FATAL (6) returned 8 hits: 6 documents with severity_num=5 and 2 with severity_num=6. All 23 documents in the window carry svc=order-276 and messages whose bracketed prefix matches the numeric code ([INFO]=3, [WARN]=4, [ERROR]=5, [FATAL]=6); the ERROR documents read "[ERROR] DB timeout N" (06:43:01Z–06:43:06Z) and the FATAL documents read "[FATAL] Disk full N" (06:44:01Z–06:44:02Z).

claims.text: Index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m exists and is green/open with docs.count 23 and store.size 9.1kb at query time (2026-11-21T06:48:06Z).
The mapping of app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m defines exactly four properties: `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer) and `svc` (keyword). No field named `level` is mapped.

`terms: {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]}` on app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned total 0 hits over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T06:48:03Z–2026-11-21T06:48:03Z (shards successful 1, failed 0); the same query over the default 1h range 2026-11-21T05:48:03Z–06:48:03Z also returned 0.
Aggregating app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m over the authorized window gives 23 total documents with severity_num buckets {3: 10, 4: 5, 5: 6, 6: 2}, and a single svc bucket {order-276: 23}.

Documents show the numeric codes correspond to message prefixes: severity_num=3 carries "[INFO] Order placed N", severity_num=4 carries "[WARN] Slow query N", severity_num=5 carries "[ERROR] DB timeout N", and severity_num=6 carries "[FATAL] Disk full N", all with svc=order-276.

Re-running the severity filter on the real field, `terms: {severity_num: [5, 6]}`, returned total 8 hits over the authorized window, with buckets severity_num=5: 6 documents and severity_num=6: 2 documents.

The ERROR-level documents in this index are six consecutive "[ERROR] DB timeout 1..6" lines at 2026-11-21T06:43:01Z–06:43:06Z, and the FATAL-level documents are two consecutive "[FATAL] Disk full 1..2" lines at 2026-11-21T06:44:01Z–06:44:02Z; the newest document in the index is 2026-11-21T06:46:10Z.

The zero result for `level` is caused solely by field naming: severity in this index is stored numerically in `severity_num`, not as a string `level`, so a string terms query on `level` can never match. The alternative hypothesis that this index held no ERROR/FATAL events at all is contradicted by the 8 documents returned under severity_num 5 and 6.

For future severity queries against app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m, filter on `severity_num` with 5 for ERROR and 6 for FATAL (4 = WARN, 3 = INFO), or search `msg` for the "[ERROR]"/"[FATAL]" prefixes; do not use a `level` field, which is not mapped in this index.
